title: CyberThreat Mesh

basics.tagline: Autonomous Cloud Threat Surface & Attack Graph Engine

listing.shortDescription: A 20-screen interactive security operations platform for visualizing cloud attack surfaces, threat paths, vulnerabilities, governance, and blast-radius analytics.
listing.fullDescription: CyberThreat Mesh is an interactive SaaS-style security product for reasoning about cloud attack surfaces. It combines a reusable SVG attack graph, autonomous-agent control surfaces, vulnerability feeds, blast-radius analytics, temporal replay, compliance reporting, RBAC governance, connector health, and audit trails in a theme-aware front-end system driven by deterministic simulated domain data.

closing.clientOverview: CyberThreat Mesh is designed for SOC analysts, threat-hunt leads, cloud security architects, and GRC auditors who need a clear operational view of identities, workloads, data stores, vulnerabilities, and attack paths. The product is a fully implemented interactive front-end system with simulated cybersecurity domain data, not a live security connector or AI runtime.
closing.conclusion: The result is a navigable, theme-coherent security product surface with 20 statically rendered routes, a reusable graph engine, responsive dashboard architecture, interactive filters and analytics, and honest boundaries around what is simulated. Its typed contracts and reusable components leave a clean path toward replacing the mock data layer with live security systems later.

features.title: Reusable attack graph engine
features.description: A deterministic SVG graph renders cloud assets, risk states, curved edges, zoom controls, filtering, and interactive node inspection across five product screens.

features.title: Dual-theme design system
features.description: Class-based light and dark themes use CSS design tokens so risk colors, badges, borders, charts, and surfaces remain coherent across the product.

features.title: Security operations workspace
features.description: Explore agent control, reasoning traces, vulnerabilities, centrality, temporal replay, investigation, compliance, RBAC, integrations, and audit logs.

features.title: Interactive graph analytics
features.description: Filters, scrubbers, node selection, two-hop investigation, blast-radius overlays, and graph-derived metrics respond to the mock dataset in the browser.

features.title: Responsive application shell
features.description: A sticky header, collapsible sidebar, isolated scroll viewport, mobile drawer, and shared UI kit keep 20 screens navigable and consistent.

features.title: Honest simulated domain layer
features.description: Typed deterministic datasets power the product experience while the case study clearly distinguishes simulated agents, telemetry, and connectors from live infrastructure.

challenge.summary: A graph-heavy security product had to make dense cloud attack-surface data feel immediate, readable, and consistent across 20 distinct workflows without relying on live backend systems.

points.title: Cluttered graph canvases
points.description: Naive graph layouts can overlap nodes, collide edges with labels, and force constant pan and zoom during security triage.

points.title: Theme-split visual language
points.description: Risk colors, badges, and charts needed to remain legible and semantically consistent in both tactical dark mode and high-contrast light mode.

points.title: Complex dashboard architecture
points.description: Twenty screens needed one reliable header, sidebar, scroll model, navigation system, and component vocabulary rather than isolated page-specific solutions.

points.title: Fast perceived performance
points.description: The product needed instant local rendering, bounded motion, and genuinely interactive charts and filters without skeleton screens or blocking states.

solution.summary: CyberThreat Mesh uses typed deterministic data, a reusable graph engine, CSS design tokens, and a shared application shell to make a complex security product fast, inspectable, and consistent.

points.title: Guaranteed graph layout
points.description: A seeded grid layout with controlled jitter guarantees at least 146px node separation while quadratic bezier paths keep edges away from labels.

points.title: Theme-aware risk tokens
points.description: CSS variables and color-mix derived tokens keep critical, high, medium, and low risk states readable across both themes and chart surfaces.

points.title: One shared application shell
points.description: AppLayout, navigation data, reusable cards, gauges, charts, terminals, drawers, and graph components amortize the cost of the 20-screen scope.

points.title: State-driven interactions
points.description: Filters, sliders, scrubbers, graph selection, investigation extraction, compliance frameworks, and pricing controls derive views from a single typed dataset.

points.title: Bounded motion and static rendering
points.description: All 70-plus animation calls stay within a 150ms motion budget, while Next.js statically prerenders the product routes for an instant first paint.

results.label: Product routes
results.detail: A complete security product surface spanning platform overview, attack graph, agents, analytics, governance, and administration.

results.label: Minimum graph spacing
results.detail: The deterministic graph layout guarantees readable node separation above the 140px specification.

results.label: Bounded animations
results.detail: More than 70 Framer Motion calls stay within the documented 150ms interaction budget.

results.label: HTTP route checks
results.detail: Every product route was smoke-tested successfully over HTTP, with production build and lint verification documented in the case study.

workflow.description: Typed mock data represents AWS IAM roles, EC2 instances, S3 buckets, Kubernetes pods, RDS databases, Azure AD principals, CVEs, and graph edges.

workflow.description: The reusable SVG engine lays out nodes deterministically, draws curved relationships, and exposes risk state, CVSS, exploitability, and MITRE context.

workflow.description: Analysts filter by IAM, unpatched CVE, S3, risk, region, and entity type, then inspect nodes or isolate two-hop investigation sub-graphs.

workflow.title: Impact and history analyzed
workflow.description: Blast radius, centrality, timeline replay, vulnerability feeds, reasoning traces, and compliance readiness derive interactive views from the shared dataset.

workflow.title: Evidence and access reviewed
workflow.description: RBAC, connector health, audit logs, and generated reports provide governance surfaces while clearly presenting simulated product data as simulated.

objectives: Implement 20 fully populated product screens across four security operations categories
Build a reusable SVG attack graph with guaranteed minimum node spacing and interactive inspection
Ship a dual-theme design system with readable risk colors in light and dark modes
Make charts, filters, sliders, scrubbers, and graph exploration genuinely interactive against typed mock data
Keep every animation within the 150ms motion budget and avoid blocking skeleton states
Verify static rendering, type safety, lint cleanliness, and HTTP health across all routes
